title: How important is it do differentiate between the therapeutic relationship and its aspects? A cross-sectional analysis of the therapeutic alliance and other process-related variables in child & adolescent psychotherapy using structure equation modeling.
summary:
The therapeutic relationship is a widely explored construct in psychotherapy process research. Often it is viewed as one of the most important factors influencing the therapeutic success. In child and adolescent psychotherapy research, the therapeutic relationship has often been viewed as one singular construct, even though past studies have found evidence for its subconstructs being at least equally important. 
The goals of this study are twofold: first we will investigate whether the inclusion of subaspects of the therapeutic relationship results in a more accurate fit of the models to the data compared to a unidimensional view of the therapeutic relationship. In a second step we will explore this research question with the inclusion of further process-related constructs (symptomatology, clinical improvement, self efficacy expectations).
conditions: All patients have a mental health disorder (at least one F-diagnosis accordng to ICD-10) and an indication for outpatient psychotherapy.

interventions.name: Patients, caregivers and therapists of a university outpatient unit for child and adolescent psychotherapy complete the rating scale BeKi (assesment of therapeutic relationship)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients currently receiving treatment at the outpatient unit for child and adolescent psychotherapy at Trier University, Germany
Exclusion criteria:
Given objection to usage of the collected data in the context of treatment for scientific purposes.
